intro.title: Identity and Social Purpose
intro.content: LAPODEV is a leading research center in human and social sciences acting as an Interface between the academic world and society. It is a center of excellence that brings together, on a voluntary basis, teacher-researchers, researchers, and experts from various disciplinary backgrounds to serve Humanity and society. The Center enjoys administrative and financial autonomy and independence.
intro.social_object: LAPODEV's social object is fundamental research and action research from an interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary, and holistic perspective.

values.title: Institutional Values and Missions
values.content: LAPODEV places Anthropos and society at the heart of its action. Its values of rigor, quality, freedom of thought, openness, social justice, and equity are reflected in its missions. It is concerned with its integrity as an autonomous research community, heir to a scientific tradition of free examination, social involvement, and civic engagement.
values.missions_label: The five institutional missions of LAPODEV are:
values.m1: Production of fundamental research and action research; Dissemination and popularization of scientific information
values.m4: Promotion of inclusion, emancipation, and empowerment of vulnerable groups
values.m5: Protection of cultural, environmental heritage, and biodiversity

objectives.title: LAPODEV Objectives
objectives.intro: To achieve its social object and missions mentioned above, LAPODEV pursues the following specific objectives:
objectives.o1: Organize and conduct scientific research and consulting on political, inclusive and sustainable development, social, cultural, and environmental issues over the long term and by varying scales (local-global)
objectives.o2: Disseminate and restore research results through publications, colloquia, seminar-courses, conferences, artistic exhibitions, and scientific workshops
objectives.o3: Assist and advise in political decision-making, the promotion of good governance, the design and planning, implementation, and evaluation of multi-sectoral public policies
objectives.o4: Promote social inclusion, emancipation, and empowerment of vulnerable groups
objectives.o5: Carry out, on behalf of third parties, through contract and remuneration, empirical and analytical research, as well as the planning, design, implementation, and evaluations of development projects and programs in all fields of social, economic, cultural, political, and environmental life
objectives.o6: Ensure the protection of peoples' cultural heritage, the environment, and biodiversity
objectives.o7: Organize and lead teachings, trainings, and internships on an individual and collective basis for capacity building and academic succession in the Democratic Republic of Congo
objectives.o8: Establish and maintain partnerships and collaborations with Universities, Centers, and Research Institutes at national and international levels to stimulate and increase incoming mobility (by hosting external researchers within LAPODEV) and outgoing mobility (by sending LAPODEV researchers to partners) for internships, specific training, and exchanges of experience

general_assembly.title: General Assembly
general_assembly.content: The General Assembly is the supreme body of LAPODEV. It is composed of Teacher-researchers, researchers, post-doctoral fellows, doctoral students, experts, partners, supporters, and students. It defines the general policy, approves research programs, and elects members of the various management bodies.

politics.title: Political Domain
politics.subtitle: Homo politicus - Elucidation of the political object
politics.intro: Given the extraordinary semantic fluidity of the word "politics", this concept is understood here in a broad sense, both according to its Greek etymology "politicus" (relating to the State) and according to the three Anglo-Saxon terms:

concepts.polity: Spaces of activities and conflicts around the question of government and the governance of society, political field or arena depending on the case.
concepts.politics: Political activity, commitment, and exercise of the political profession; capacity of certain groups of individuals to direct life in society and to produce rules that apply to everyone.
concepts.policy: Public action, public policy in a particular sector, and decisions taken by those who exercise the functions of government.

goals: Study power structures, modes of governance, and relations between the State and society through a cultural and historical perspective
Analyze how beliefs, practices, and institutions influence power and authority in different societies and contexts
Understand real and daily political functioning through contextualized analysis of multiple actor interactions from local to global
Examine the dynamics of political power relations based on ethnographic observation of practices and public policies
Understand the diversity of political organizational forms and the dynamics of social and political change

development.title: Domain of Sustainable and Inclusive Development
development.intro: LAPODEV, as an Interface between the academic world and Congolese society, is relevant for understanding the dynamics that influence sustainable development.
development.quote: Political and development anthropology offers a unique perspective for analyzing the interactions between political institutions, social actors, and development processes.
goals: Understand the root causes and problems of underdevelopment (inequalities, conflicts, corruption, governance)
Design more appropriate and acceptable development strategies, projects, and programs for local populations
Strengthen civic participation by involving local communities in design and implementation
Evaluate the real impact of development projects and programs on local populations
Contribute to the consolidation of peace and security through conflict prevention and the promotion of good governance

vulnerabilities.title: Domain of Vulnerability Analysis
vulnerabilities.intro: LAPODEV analyzes vulnerability factors for holistic management and a better understanding of inequalities.
goals: Analyze and take vulnerability into account for holistic management via a participatory approach
Better understand inequalities and factors that increase risks for certain populations
Identify and study so-called "vulnerable" social groups and community resilience
Promote social participation, emancipation, and empowerment of vulnerable groups
Design targeted interventions to reduce vulnerability and promote inclusion

groups.children: Children in difficult situations (abandoned, street children, disabled, associated with armed conflict, or in conflict with the law)
groups.minorities: Indigenous peoples, ethnic, racial, or religious minorities victims of discrimination
groups.women: Teenage mothers, battered women, divorced, raped, sexual slaves, or widows with children
groups.handicap_hiv_lgbt: People living with disabilities (barriers to services), with HIV (stigmatization), and LGBT+ people (discrimination and violence)
groups.displaced: Internally displaced persons, refugees, people in extreme poverty, homeless, or victims of disasters and wars

bios.indeka: Joseph Indeka Nkoso is a Full Professor in the Department of Anthropology and Director of LAPODEV. Aggregated in history, he holds a PhD in Political and Social Sciences from the Université Libre de Bruxelles. His research reconciles multidisciplinarity, scale variation, and long duration.
bios.kavira: PhD in Systematics from the Faculté Universitaire de Théologie Protestante de Bruxelles. Specialist in Gender Studies. Author of several articles and researcher at LAPODEV.
